```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(agecraft)
```

## Calculate calendar ages

Use an explicit reference date for reproducible reporting.

```{r calendar}
birth <- as.Date(c("2020-02-29", "1980-04-14", "2010-09-15", NA))
reference <- as.Date("2025-03-01")
age <- calculate_age(birth, reference, "year")
age
```

Leap birthdays reach their next year on March 1 in non-leap years. Reversed dates
raise an error. Missing observations remain missing. Months use calendar
anniversaries, including the last day of short months; elapsed-day conversion
with the units package is an approximation of calendar months or years.

## Assign reporting groups

```{r groups}
groups <- as.age_group(age.groups$Annual, unit = "year")
category <- age_cat_iv(age, groups)
data.frame(birth, age, category)
table(category, useNA = "ifany")
```

The bundled groups are preserved from the original rage package. They are legacy
reporting conventions and should be confirmed against the reporting system's
current specification. The package records their available provenance without
claiming an unverified official version or endorsement.

## Resolve overlaps explicitly

```{r overlaps}
overlapping <- as.age_group(c("0-9", "5-14"), unit = "year")
age_cat_iv(units::set_units(c(3, 7, 12), "year"), overlapping, multiple = "first")
```

The default `multiple = "error"` rejects ambiguity. `first` and `last` refer to
sorted interval order, not the original input order.

## Keep units explicit

```{r units}
days <- calculate_age(as.Date("2025-01-01"), as.Date("2025-02-15"), "day")
day_groups <- as.age_group(c(0, 7, 14, 30, 60, Inf), unit = "day")
age_cat_iv(days, day_groups)
```

Both sides must have units or both must be unitless. `convert_units` selects which
side to convert. Conversions between month/year and smaller units require
`allow_approx = TRUE`; calculate ages directly in the reporting unit when possible.

## Combine observations safely

```{r combine}
one <- as.age_group(c("0-4", "5-9"), unit = "year")
two <- as.age_group("10-14", unit = "year")
vctrs::vec_c(one, two)
generics::as.ordered(one[c(2, 1)])
```

Concatenation preserves class and units; incompatible units raise an error.
Ordered factor conversion keeps observation order and sorts the factor levels.
